paragraphs.text: This loose tea comes from [Anhua](anhua:where-it-is), a county of hills and steep valleys on the middle Zi river in north-central Hunan, at the northern foot of the Xuefeng mountains, where rice is hard to grow and tea does well. The same warm, wet air that grows the leaf is the air it is piled and aged in, which is why the trade ties [the character of Anhua tea](anhua:why-people-value-it) to the place as much as to the method.

Like all [dark tea](dark:definition), it is left to change in warmth and moisture after the leaf is made, as microbes and the leaf's own chemistry slowly darken it. In Anhua every tea begins as one raw tea, [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), from large local leaf that is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried, then steamed soft before it is shaped.

Made in 2023, it is three years old. Anhua tea is [kept for years](anhua-dark:ageing) and said to improve, though no agreed count of years marks it as aged. It wants a clean, dry, aired place, away from mould and other smells.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
